content.value_statement: Competitive search pages often become shallow tables that buyers distrust. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create fair, research-based alternative pages.
actual_capabilities: Defines four page formats: singular alternatives, plural alternatives, product versus competitor, and competitor versus competitor.
Provides page structures, target keywords, tone guidance, and URL patterns for each format.
Shows how to centralize competitor data for pricing, features, strengths, weaknesses, and migration notes.
Includes reusable section templates for summaries, feature comparisons, pricing, support, migration, and social proof.
Gives research steps for product testing, pricing checks, review mining, customer feedback, and competitor messaging.
Outlines SEO considerations, internal linking, index pages, FAQ schema, and page set planning.
limitations: It does not verify competitor claims without current research from the user or web sources.
It does not generate live search volume, pricing, or review data by itself.
It cannot guarantee rankings or conversions after pages are published.
It focuses on page strategy and copy, not technical site deployment.

use_cases.title: Plan SEO Comparison Pages
use_cases.description: Create a prioritized set of alternative and versus pages for competitors with clear search intent and page structure.

use_cases.title: Support Sales Evaluation
use_cases.description: Build fair comparison content that helps prospects understand tradeoffs, migration effort, pricing, and fit.

use_cases.title: Maintain Competitor Data
use_cases.description: Create a reusable competitor data source so pricing, features, and positioning stay consistent across pages.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Simple Alternative Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to draft a [Competitor] alternative page for [Product]. Include search intent, page outline, key sections, and CTA ideas.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Fair Versus Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to write a [Product] vs [Competitor] page. Compare features, pricing, support, fit, migration, and honest tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Competitor Data Profile
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to create a competitor data profile for [Competitor]. Include positioning, pricing, features, strengths, weaknesses, complaints, and migration notes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Comparison Page Program
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to plan a full comparison page set for [Product]. Prioritize competitors, index pages, internal links, update cadence, and schema opportunities.

output_examples.input: Create a Notion alternative page outline for a project management tool.
output: Search intent: users want a more structured project management workflow than Notion.
Recommended sections: pain points, quick summary, feature comparison, pricing context, migration path, and customer proof.
Positioning note: acknowledge Notion flexibility before explaining where the product is stronger.

output_examples.input: Compare our product with a direct competitor for sales enablement.
output: Opening summary: state the main tradeoff in two clear sentences.
Comparison areas: features, pricing, support, ease of use, integrations, and migration.
Fit guidance: name who should choose each product and why.

output_examples.input: Plan a competitor comparison content program.
output: Priority list: start with direct competitors that have clear search demand.
Content set: create alternative pages, versus pages, index pages, and selected head-to-head comparisons.
Maintenance plan: refresh pricing quarterly and update competitor data after major launches.

best_practices: Verify pricing, feature claims, and review themes before publishing any comparison page.
Name competitor strengths clearly so readers trust the recommendation.
Keep competitor data centralized and refresh it on a fixed schedule.
anti_patterns: Do not publish thin pages that only contain feature checklists.
Do not hide meaningful competitor advantages or your own limitations.
Do not reuse stale pricing or review claims across many pages.

faq.question: What page types does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports alternative pages, alternatives roundups, direct versus pages, and competitor versus competitor pages.

faq.question: Can it help with SEO planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes keyword intent, URL patterns, index pages, internal links, and FAQ schema guidance.

faq.question: Does it require competitor research?
faq.answer: Yes. The strongest output depends on current product, pricing, review, and customer evidence.

faq.question: Can it write fair comparison copy?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends acknowledging competitor strengths and explaining tradeoffs instead of using one-sided claims.

faq.question: Does it create technical site code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on content strategy, page structure, copy, and reusable data planning.

faq.question: Who should use it?
faq.answer: Growth, content, SEO, and sales teams can use it to create trustworthy competitive landing pages.
